newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Jan 19.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Former Prime Minister and opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia on Saturday said that her Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) would exploit all opportunities available in and outside the parliament to protest "persecution" of opposition political activists.
Experts from India and Bangladesh began monitoring the flow of the Ganges water at the Bangladesh side of the common river.
President Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed called for a "social resistance" against loan defaulters and advised political parties not to harbour them.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina is expected to have a meeting with President Bill Clinton to discuss bilateral matters during her visit to Washington early next month to attend the World Micro-credit Summit.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalists Party (BNP) and Jmaat-e-Islami have decided not to contest the Thakurgaon byelection on the plea that voting will not be fair under the present Chief Election Commissioner and the party in power.
A top U.S. company signed a production-sharing contract with the state-run Petrobangla on Saturday for exploration of oil and gas in sea.
Indian border security forces allegedly shot dead a Bangladeshi youngman on Friday at the northern Lalmonirhat frontier.
